name: Ningbo Lishe International Airport
before:
Ningbo's airport, serving Zhejiang's second city and the southern side of the Yangtze River Delta. It handled 16.1 million passengers in 2025, thirtieth in China, and is twenty seventh for cargo.

Getting into the city is easy and partly free. A free bus runs between the terminal and Lishe International Airport station every ten minutes, limousine coaches run hourly into downtown Ningbo, and less frequent services reach the wider prefectures.

The terminal opened in October 2002 with 16 departure gates and seven jetways, and the airport has been expanded repeatedly since, with a flight area expansion in 2006 and a third phase from 2015.

It has an unexpected place in aviation history. Lishe was an auxiliary base of the Nationalist Chinese Air Force and the final launching point for the Martin B-10 bombers that flew the transoceanic raid on Nagasaki and other Japanese cities on 19 and 20 May 1938.

The airport opened to the public in June 1990 as the first civil-only airport in Zhejiang and took its international name in November 2005.
after:
The airport for Ningbo, in Zhejiang. In 2025 it handled 16.1 million passengers, 30th in China, while its cargo ranked 27th.

Line 2 of the Ningbo metro starts at Lishe International Airport station.
